subject: Startups
title: Customer Lifetime Value
description: A micro-lesson that makes Customer Lifetime Value usable.

hook.text: A customer isn't worth what they pay this month. They're worth what they'll pay over years of staying with you.

buildup.text: LTV estimates total revenue a customer generates. It's ARPU divided by monthly churn rate, simplified.

discovery.text: Amazon Prime members spend $1,400 per year vs. $600 for non-members. Prime's LTV is more than double.

twist.text: LTV is a prediction, not a fact. If churn changes, LTV changes. Founders who treat LTV as fixed get burned.

climax.text: The goal is simple: make LTV go up (better product) and CAC go down (better marketing). The gap is your profit.

punchline.text: LTV is the promise. Retention is what keeps it.

quiz.question: What key factor determines LTV?
options: How long customers stay and how much they spend
